sermon.title: A Quick Change of Government 11/26/2017
sermon.speaker: Unnamed speaker (not Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: This message tells how King Hezekiah inherited a nation ruined by his father Ahaz and turned it around quickly: he reopened the temple doors, cleansed out the filth, restored priests, offerings and David’s pattern of worship, and called all Israel to Passover. Despite mockery, a few humbled themselves, idols came down, tithing returned, and God delivered Judah from Assyria.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Church members addressed by first name are in the transcript only. Garbled names left as [unclear] (e.g. the Assyrian king at 41:42, Asaph at 28:10). Misnamed reference kept as spoken: “2nd Chronicles 12:32” for 2 Chronicles 30:12 (35:40). Points to check: “7 billion people on the planet”; Christmas “December 21st 25th”. Sensitive content kept as spoken: people who “totally turned their backs given God the finger”; “stuck as a homosexual”; leaders and teachers; the church mocked as “a bunch of dopes”, “idiots”.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah and broke the sacred pillars in pieces, cut down the wooden images, and threw down the high places and the altars—from all Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh—until they had utterly destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel returned to their own cities, every man to his possession.

Then the LORD sent an angel who cut down every mighty man of valor, leader, and captain in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned shamefaced to his own land. And when he had gone into the temple of his god, some of his own offspring struck him down with the sword there.
And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, in the law and in the commandment, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart. So he prospered.

faqs.question: What did Hezekiah inherit?
faqs.answer: A sinful nation and a moral mess.

faqs.question: What had they done to the temple doors?
What did Hezekiah make with the Lord?
When did Hezekiah begin his reforms?
faqs.answer: In the first month of his first year.

faqs.answer: God sent an angel and destroyed it.
